guide.title: Mass-Casualty Incidents & Triage
guide.lead: When patients outnumber resources, the goal changes from the best for each to the most for all. The first crew sets up command, declares the incident and calls for help before treating anyone. Triage quickly, fix only what kills in seconds, and keep re-triaging.

steps.title: Declare and request
steps.text: Announce a mass-casualty incident and send a METHANE report; ask for more ambulances early.

steps.title: Command
steps.text: Take command until relieved; set up triage, treatment and transport areas and staging.

steps.title: Triage, don't treat
steps.text: Move through everyone; only life-saving actions as you go.
Not breathing: open the airway. Still not breathing: black. Breathing now: red.
No radial pulse or capillary refill over 2 seconds

sections.title: JumpSTART (children)
items: For children who look under about 8 years
Not breathing but has a pulse: 5 rescue breaths – breathing returns: red; still not: black
Red if respiratory rate below 15 or above 45/min, no palpable pulse, or inappropriate response to pain (AVPU P or U)

sections.title: Colours
rows: Life threat that can be fixed now

quiz.q: First EMS unit at a mass-casualty incident should first:
options: Establish command, declare the incident and request resources
quiz.explanation: Without help coming, triage won't matter.

quiz.q: START: not walking, RR 28/min, radial pulse present, doesn't follow commands. Tag?
quiz.explanation: Can't follow commands is a red criterion.

quiz.q: JumpSTART: a 6-year-old is not breathing but has a pulse. You:
options: Give 5 rescue breaths: breathing returns → red; if not → black
quiz.explanation: Children often arrest from breathing problems.

quiz.q: Walking woman looking for her daughter, small forearm cut. Tag and action?
options: Green: send her to the green area
RR above 30, no radial pulse or refill over 2 seconds, can't follow commands

quiz.q: In START, the first step that shrinks the patient pool:
options: Ask everyone who can walk to move to a set area

quiz.q: JumpSTART respiratory rate that makes a child red:

options: The greatest good for the greatest number
quiz.explanation: Resources go where they save most lives.

quiz.q: During triage you may stop to:
options: Apply a tourniquet or open an airway

flashcards.question: Mass-casualty incident
flashcards.answer: Any event where patients outnumber the available resources (people, equipment, transport).

flashcards.question: RPM in START
flashcards.answer: Respirations above 30/min, Perfusion (no radial pulse or refill over 2 seconds), Mental status (can't follow commands): any one = red.

flashcards.question: Triage colours
flashcards.answer: Red: immediate. Yellow: delayed. Green: minor (walking wounded). Black: dead or expectant.

flashcards.question: First step in START
flashcards.answer: Everyone who can walk goes to a set area: green.

flashcards.question: JumpSTART
flashcards.answer: For children under about 8: 5 rescue breaths for a child not breathing with a pulse; red if RR below 15 or above 45/min, no pulse, or P/U on AVPU.

flashcards.question: Disaster triage principle
flashcards.answer: The greatest good for the greatest number.

critical.scenario: First unit at a highway crash with a school bus and two cars: about 30 patients, chaos, people screaming and wandering.
critical.question: Sequence of actions?

options.t: Safety, declare a mass-casualty incident with a METHANE report and request resources, take command, set up areas and staging, then START triage
Load two red patients and leave

options.f: The first unit leads until relieved.

critical.explanation: The first 10 minutes shape the whole incident.
critical.kpi: Initiates MCI command, notification and triage

critical.scenario: Building collapse: you've triaged 22 patients. A yellow patient is now breathing 34/min and confused.
critical.question: What do you do?

options.t: Re-triage to red and move him to the red area: triage is continuous
Treat him in place for 20 minutes

critical.explanation: Re-triage at every handover and transfer.
critical.kpi: Recognizes the dynamic nature of triage

critical.scenario: Shooting with 15 victims, scene secure. Three reds: a sucking chest wound with distress; a leg wound with a tourniquet, now stable; an abdominal wound with shock.
critical.question: Transport order?

options.t: Seal the chest wound (vented seal) and send him first; then the abdominal wound in shock; the controlled leg wound last of the reds
Leg wound first: it was bleeding most

critical.explanation: Distribute patients so no hospital is overwhelmed.
